poses.name: Mountain Pose
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart and soften your knees.
Lengthen through the crown of your head; let shoulders relax.
Breathe naturally and feel both feet grounded.
poses.modifications: Stand near a wall or sit tall in a chair.
poses.contraindications: Generally gentle; stand or sit if balance feels unsteady.

poses.name: Tree Pose
steps: Stand near a wall or chair.
Place one foot at the ankle or calf; avoid pressing on the knee.
Bring hands together or keep one hand supported; switch sides.
poses.benefits: Practises balance, focus, and leg strength.
poses.modifications: Keep toes on the floor like a kickstand; hold a chair.
poses.contraindications: Skip balancing if dizzy or unsafe to stand.

poses.name: Triangle Pose
steps: Take a comfortable wide stance; turn one foot out.
Reach over that leg and rest a hand on your thigh or a block.
Lengthen both sides of your waist; repeat on the other side.
poses.modifications: Use a wall or chair; keep range small.
poses.contraindications: Avoid deep reaches with acute back, hip, or balance concerns.

poses.name: Warrior I
steps: Step feet apart and turn the front foot forward.
Bend the front knee only as much as comfortable, tracking it over the foot.
Keep hands on hips or raise arms; change sides.
poses.benefits: Builds comfortable leg strength and stability.
poses.modifications: Shorten stance, use a chair, or keep hands at hips.
poses.contraindications: Reduce depth for knee or hip discomfort; avoid pain.

poses.name: Warrior II
steps: Stand wide with front toes pointing forward and back toes slightly in.
Bend the front knee gently; keep torso upright.
Rest hands on hips or extend arms; switch sides.
poses.benefits: Practises leg endurance and body awareness.
poses.modifications: Use a shorter stance or chair support.
poses.contraindications: Modify for knee, hip, or balance concerns.

poses.name: Warrior III
steps: Stand by a wall or chair and shift weight to one foot.
Hinge forward a little as the other leg reaches back.
Keep hands supported; return slowly and switch.
poses.modifications: Keep back toes on floor; use two-hand support.
poses.contraindications: Avoid unsupported balance with dizziness or fall risk.

poses.name: Chair Pose
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart.
Send hips back a little as if reaching for a chair.
Keep knees comfortable and hands on thighs or raised.
poses.modifications: Practise sitting-to-standing with a real chair.
poses.contraindications: Keep shallow or skip if knees or hips hurt.

poses.name: Extended Side Angle
steps: Take a comfortable side lunge with front knee softly bent.
Rest forearm on thigh or hand on a block.
Reach the other arm overhead only if comfortable; switch sides.
poses.modifications: Use chair support and a shorter stance.
poses.contraindications: Avoid deep lunges with knee, hip, or balance problems.

poses.name: Half Moon
steps: Place a block or hand on a wall in front of you.
Shift weight to one foot and open the other leg only as high as steady.
Keep gaze down; lower slowly and switch.
poses.modifications: Keep back toes on floor or practise at a wall.
poses.contraindications: Skip unsupported balance with dizziness or fall risk.

poses.name: Easy Pose
steps: Sit on a folded blanket or chair.
Cross legs only if comfortable and stack shoulders over hips.
Rest hands on thighs and breathe easily.
poses.benefits: Comfortable position for breathing and quiet focus.
poses.modifications: Sit in a chair or elevate hips.
poses.contraindications: Do not force crossed legs with knee or hip discomfort.

poses.name: Thunderbolt Pose
steps: Kneel on a padded surface only if comfortable.
Sit back toward heels or place a block between heels and hips.
Keep spine easy and breathe; come out slowly.
poses.benefits: A stable seated option for some practitioners.
poses.modifications: Sit on a chair; add padding or a block.
poses.contraindications: Avoid kneeling with knee, ankle, or circulation discomfort.

poses.name: Lotus Pose
steps: Only if already comfortable, sit tall and place legs in a loose cross.
Do not pull feet onto thighs or force knees down.
Uncross gently and change leg position.
poses.benefits: Traditional meditation seat; no special benefit is guaranteed.
poses.modifications: Use Easy Pose or a chair instead.
poses.contraindications: Avoid if any knee, hip, or ankle discomfort; never force.

poses.name: Staff Pose
steps: Sit with legs forward, knees softly bent if needed.
Place hands beside hips or on blocks.
Sit tall without locking knees; breathe steadily.
poses.modifications: Sit against a wall or bend knees.
poses.contraindications: Use support if hamstrings or lower back feel strained.

poses.name: Seated Forward Bend
steps: Sit on a folded blanket with knees soft.
Hinge slightly from hips; rest hands on thighs or shins.
Keep neck relaxed and stop well before strain.
poses.modifications: Bend knees, use a strap, or stay upright.
poses.contraindications: Skip deep folding with acute back pain or pregnancy; choose supported upright rest.

poses.name: Head-to-Knee Pose
steps: Sit with one leg extended and the other foot resting comfortably inward.
Lengthen spine; hinge a little toward the extended leg.
Stay upright if needed; change sides.
poses.modifications: Bend extended knee and use a strap.
poses.contraindications: Avoid deep fold with acute back pain or pregnancy.

poses.name: Half Lord of the Fishes
steps: Sit tall with both legs comfortable.
Turn gently from the ribs, keeping the twist small and easy.
Release to centre and repeat on the other side.
poses.modifications: Sit on a chair; keep hips facing forward and twist minimally.
poses.contraindications: Avoid deep twists with pregnancy, disc symptoms, or acute back pain.

poses.name: Bound Angle Pose
steps: Sit on a blanket and bring soles of feet near one another.
Let knees rest naturally; do not press them down.
Sit upright or lean back on cushions.
poses.modifications: Place cushions under thighs or sit in a chair.
poses.contraindications: Avoid forcing range with hip, groin, or knee pain.

poses.name: Cobra Pose
steps: Lie on belly with hands under shoulders, or rest forehead on hands.
Press lightly and lift chest only a little, keeping elbows bent.
Lower with control; repeat only if comfortable.
poses.benefits: Gentle front-body opening and back awareness.
poses.modifications: Keep forehead down or practise seated chest opening.
poses.contraindications: Skip if it causes back pain, during pregnancy, or after abdominal surgery without clearance.

poses.name: Bow Pose
steps: Lie on belly; bend knees only if comfortable.
Reach for ankles only if easy; lift minimally without pulling.
Release immediately and rest.
poses.benefits: Strong backbend challenge; not needed for a balanced practice.
poses.modifications: Practise a small one-leg-at-a-time lift or skip.
poses.contraindications: Avoid in pregnancy, back/neck pain, hernia, or recent abdominal surgery.

poses.name: Bridge Pose
steps: Lie on back with knees bent and feet grounded.
Press feet gently and lift hips a comfortable amount.
Lower slowly; pause if breath or back feels strained.
poses.modifications: Lift only a little or place a block under hips for supported rest.
poses.contraindications: Avoid if it worsens neck or back pain; keep neck still.

poses.name: Camel Pose
steps: Kneel on padding with hands on hips.
Lengthen upward and lean back slightly, keeping head neutral.
Return upright slowly; hands need not reach heels.
poses.modifications: Keep hands on hips and make a tiny lean.
poses.contraindications: Avoid for neck/back pain, dizziness, pregnancy, or uncontrolled blood pressure.

poses.name: Wheel Pose
steps: This demanding pose is for experienced practitioners with appropriate instruction.
Use a prepared, pain-free setup; never push into a backbend.
Exit carefully and rest.
poses.modifications: Choose Bridge Pose instead.
poses.contraindications: Avoid with neck/back/wrist issues, pregnancy, blood-pressure or heart concerns, or without suitable guidance.

poses.name: Locust Pose
steps: Lie on belly with forehead supported and arms by sides.
Lengthen legs; lift one leg a little, then lower and switch.
Keep breath easy and neck relaxed.
poses.modifications: Lift one leg at a time or skip lifting.
poses.contraindications: Skip if it causes back pain, during pregnancy, or after recent abdominal surgery.

poses.name: Standing Forward Fold
steps: Stand with knees soft and hands on thighs.
Hinge only a little; hands may rest on a chair or blocks.
Rise slowly, especially if prone to dizziness.
poses.modifications: Use a chair and keep torso lifted.
poses.contraindications: Avoid deep folding with pregnancy, glaucoma, uncontrolled blood pressure, or dizziness.

poses.name: Downward-Facing Dog
steps: Start on hands and knees with hands supported.
Lift hips only if comfortable; keep knees bent and head relaxed.
Return to hands and knees before strain.
poses.modifications: Use a wall or chair; stay on hands and knees.
poses.contraindications: Skip with wrist/shoulder pain, glaucoma, uncontrolled blood pressure, or pregnancy if uncomfortable.

poses.name: Shoulder Stand
steps: An advanced inversion requiring qualified in-person instruction.
Do not turn or load the neck; choose a restorative alternative.
poses.benefits: Traditional inversion; not necessary for wellbeing.
poses.modifications: Legs-up-the-wall with hips supported, if comfortable.
poses.contraindications: Avoid with neck injury, glaucoma, pregnancy, high blood pressure, or cardiovascular conditions.

poses.name: Plow Pose
steps: Advanced inversion for qualified in-person instruction only.
Never compress or turn the neck; come out with guidance.
poses.benefits: Traditional advanced pose; no need to practise it.
poses.modifications: Choose comfortable supine rest.
poses.contraindications: Avoid with neck injury, glaucoma, pregnancy, high blood pressure, or cardiovascular concerns.

poses.name: Legs-Up-the-Wall
steps: Sit sideways beside a wall and lower to your side.
Bring legs up the wall only if comfortable; head and neck stay relaxed.
Come out slowly by rolling to your side.
poses.modifications: Rest calves on a chair instead of using a wall.
poses.contraindications: Skip if it worsens symptoms, causes numbness, or is unsuitable for your condition; ask a clinician if unsure.

poses.name: Headstand
poses.duration: Not for solo or beginner practice
steps: Advanced inversion only with qualified in-person supervision and appropriate preparation.
Never kick up, load the head/neck, or practise from app instructions alone.
poses.modifications: Choose Mountain Pose or supported rest.
poses.contraindications: Avoid with neck issues, glaucoma, high blood pressure, pregnancy, cardiovascular concerns, or any fall risk.

poses.name: Eagle Pose
steps: Stand near a wall and soften knees.
Cross arms or legs only as far as comfortable; no need to bind.
Keep gaze steady; switch sides.
poses.modifications: Keep toes on floor and hug arms across chest.
poses.contraindications: Skip balancing with dizziness; avoid joint binding that hurts.

poses.name: Dancer Pose
steps: Hold a wall or chair and stand tall.
Bend one knee and hold the foot only if easy; keep torso upright.
Release and change sides.
poses.modifications: Keep toes on floor, use a strap, or practise standing tall.
poses.contraindications: Avoid unsupported balance with fall risk or painful shoulders/knees.

poses.name: Crow Pose
steps: An optional arm balance best learned with a qualified teacher.
Use padding and keep gaze forward; never jump or force wrists.
Stop at the first sign of discomfort.
poses.modifications: Practise a supported squat with feet on floor.
poses.contraindications: Avoid with wrist/shoulder injury, pregnancy, or fall concerns.

poses.name: Child's Pose
steps: Kneel on padding or sit in a chair.
Rest torso on cushions or thighs only if comfortable.
Breathe normally; come up slowly.
poses.benefits: Resting position and gentle back relaxation.
poses.modifications: Use a chair, cushions, or lie on your side.
poses.contraindications: Skip kneeling or forward compression during pregnancy or if knees/hips are uncomfortable.

poses.name: Corpse Pose
steps: Lie on your back or sit supported.
Let the floor or chair support you; keep breathing natural.
Move fingers and toes before sitting up slowly.
poses.modifications: Side-lying or seated relaxation.
poses.contraindications: Choose another position if lying flat is uncomfortable or medically unsuitable.

poses.name: Reclined Bound Angle
steps: Lie back on cushions with knees bent.
Let knees open only as far as comfortable, supported by pillows.
Bring legs together to exit slowly.
poses.modifications: Keep knees together or rest calves on a chair.
poses.contraindications: Avoid unsupported hip opening if painful; use side-lying rest during pregnancy.

poses.name: Sun Salutation
steps: 1. Stand in Tadasana. 2. Inhale, raise arms. 3. Exhale, fold with soft knees. 4. Inhale, lengthen halfway. 5. Step back to a supported plank or hands-and-knees. 6. Lower knees/chest gently. 7. Inhale to a small Cobra or stay low. 8. Exhale to hands-and-knees or Down Dog. 9. Step forward. 10. Lengthen halfway. 11. Fold softly. 12. Rise to stand.
poses.benefits: A flowing movement sequence that can build coordination and warmth.
poses.modifications: Use a chair, skip plank/lowering, step rather than jump, and move at a comfortable pace.
poses.contraindications: Avoid forceful flow with pain, dizziness, pregnancy unless modified with qualified guidance, or uncontrolled blood pressure.

poses.name: Moon Salutation
steps: Move slowly through a gentle side-to-side sequence: Mountain, side stretch, wide-legged stance, supported side lunge, centre, and return to Mountain on the other side.
Keep transitions small and breathe comfortably.
Skip any step that feels uncomfortable.
poses.modifications: Use a chair or wall and avoid deep lunges.
poses.contraindications: Modify for balance, knee, hip, or back concerns.

breathing.name: Anulom Vilom
breathing.safety: Alternate-nostril breathing, gentle and unforced. Skip breath holds; stop if light-headed.

breathing.name: Kapalbhati
breathing.safety: Forceful exhalation practice, not a beginner relaxation breath. Avoid in pregnancy, uncontrolled blood pressure, heart conditions, hernia, recent surgery, or if unsure; seek qualified instruction.

breathing.name: Bhramari
breathing.safety: Soft humming exhale; keep volume comfortable and breathe normally between rounds.

breathing.name: Bhastrika
breathing.safety: Forceful breathing; avoid in pregnancy, uncontrolled blood pressure, heart conditions, dizziness, or if unsure. Learn with a qualified teacher.

breathing.name: Ujjayi
breathing.safety: Optional soft, comfortable breath; never constrict or strain the throat.

breathing.name: Sheetali
breathing.safety: Gentle cooling breath if comfortable; stop if it feels unpleasant or causes dizziness.

breathing.name: Sitkari
breathing.safety: Gentle cooling breath if comfortable; keep breathing easy.

breathing.name: Nadi Shodhana
breathing.safety: Slow alternate-nostril breathing without retention; stop if uncomfortable.

breathing.name: Box breathing
breathing.safety: Use comfortable, short counts; omit holds if breath holding is uncomfortable.

breathing.name: 4-7-8 breathing
breathing.safety: Optional; shorten or omit holds and never force a long breath hold.

breathing.name: Deep belly breathing
breathing.safety: Let the breath stay natural and comfortable; stop if dizzy.

meditation: Trataka (gentle steady gaze; avoid eye strain)

cleansing.name: Jala Neti
cleansing.safety: Nasal irrigation needs sterile/distilled or previously boiled and cooled water, clean equipment, and correct instruction. Not suitable for everyone; ask a clinician if you have concerns. Never use untreated tap water.

cleansing.name: Kapalbhati
cleansing.safety: Forceful breathing, not a cleansing treatment. Avoid in pregnancy, uncontrolled blood pressure, heart conditions, hernia, recent surgery, or if unsure.

quickTricks: Gentle eye breaks (look away from screens)
